title: JFrog API key header and password positions holding placeholders, references, masked text or the documented pattern as prose
summary: The header name with no value, a placeholder, an environment reference, a masked display and a username with no password, in the positions JFrog documents for an API key, and the documented API key pattern written out as prose.
rationale: A header or password position with nothing in it has nothing to protect, an angle-bracket placeholder and an environment reference stand in for a value kept elsewhere, and a masked display has no recoverable value. The documented pattern, written as text that describes the leading characters and the count of alphanumerics, is a description of a format and not a value of it. Protecting any of these would redact text a reader needs to understand how the credential is configured.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#246). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Not flagged under project policy: the texts here are empty positions, placeholders, references, masked text or a described pattern, not credential values. That a placeholder, reference or described pattern is not a value is a project decision, not a JFrog statement.

sources.supports: Artifactory allows authentication for REST API calls using your API key as an alternative to your username and password in two ways: either by using the `X-JFrog-Art-API` header with which you can specify an API key, or through basic authentication using your username and API key (instead of your password).
API Keys follow this pattern: .*\bAKCp[A-Za-z0-9]{69}\b.*, starting with AKCp and including 69 alphanumeric characters.
sources.locator: Comparing Identity Reference Tokens With API Keys
